html:
Italian Eritrea was the colony Italy proclaimed on 1 January 1890 on the Red Sea coast and the highlands north of the Mareb river, giving the country its name and borders.

The name came from the Greek for the Red Sea. After the defeat at Adwa in 1896, Italy accepted the Mareb as the border with Ethiopia. Its rulers built roads, the railway and towns, took land for settlers, and recruited a large share of Eritrean men as colonial soldiers.

Fifty years apart from Ethiopia gave Eritreans a separate identity. In the 1930s Asmara boomed as the base for the invasion of Ethiopia. British forces took the colony in 1941 and ran it until the federation with Ethiopia of 1952.
sum: Italian Eritrea was the colony Italy proclaimed on 1 January 1890 on the Red Sea coast and the highlands north of the Mareb river, giving the country its name and borders.
